reviewScope: Only uncommitted provider-free startup fixture/test diff and exact published CLI creation semantics; author worktree read-only.

findings.title: Deliver update after session ownership is established and before creation returns
findings.evidence: Published acpx 0.19.4 queue-owner-runtime-C0wIYowh.js runOnce accepts config updates only when client.hasReusableSession(notification.sessionId). AcpClient.createSession sets loadedSessionId after awaiting session/new result, then awaits captureAgentDescendants. The updated fixture sends notification before response, so it is pre-ownership and intentionally ignored. Trace proves send order, not accepted owned callback order. Parent published-controls-order-fix.log confirms 18 passed / 3 failed: every startup case rejects fixture-model with only old-model advertised.
findings.fix: Use a deterministic creation-time descendant-capture seam or another justified provider-free barrier: reply first, establish matching loaded session, deliver owned notification while createSession completion is held, then release. Assert accepted notification/control outcome order; preserve no-provider execution, cleanup assertions and existing timeouts.

findings.title: Removal scenario must initially advertise the requested model
findings.evidence: Both startup and removed initial snapshots contain only old-model while CLI requests fixture-model. The removed case expects model failure and zero prompts, which succeeds from the stale snapshot alone without processing the empty update. It cannot detect resurrection of withdrawn support.
findings.fix: For the removed scenario, advertise fixture-model exact target in the initial snapshot, then deliver an owned empty catalog during creation. Assert rejection with zero setter and prompt calls. Keep the startup initial snapshot old-only so the added-support case still detects stale overwrite.

rejected.claim: Removed-case pass proves an empty catalog removed model support
rejected.reason: The requested model was already absent from the creation catalog.
